tool.name: CreateArrayAlongAxes

summary.para:
View online help files: https://www.jennessent.com/geometric-tools/create-array-along-axes.html
Copies the input features (a layer's selection is honored) along an axis -- so many copies forward and so many backward -- and optionally along a second axis to the right and left, each step being the features' own extent along that axis plus a separation distance, so the copies in a row never overlap (rows along a second axis stay clear when the axes are perpendicular; at a narrow angle between the axes they can overlap -- widen the angle or add separation). The copies can be clipped to selected polygons, and written as a feature class and/or added to the map as graphics. In the Create Array along Axes window the source is a selected graphic and the axes are drawn on the map with a live preview. A port of the CropCentric Create Graphic Array tool (Jenness and Wiebers 2018). Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
The step. Along each axis the copies step by the source's extent along that axis plus the separation, so a 40 m wide plot with a 5 m separation repeats every 45 m. Several selected features are copied together as one group, and the step uses the group's extent. Steps are measured along the ground (geodesic), in an azimuthal equidistant projection centered on the source.
The axes. A bearing is degrees clockwise from north: copies forward go that way, backward the opposite way. The second axis defaults to the first plus 90 degrees; copies to the right go along it and to the left the opposite way. The original stays in place and is written too (Axis_1_ID and Axis_2_ID = 0).
Clipping. With clip polygons (their selection honored), every copy is cut to them and copies lying entirely outside are dropped.
Outputs. Array_ID, Axis_1_ID and Axis_2_ID (step numbers, negative backward and to the left), Source_FID (the input feature's ObjectID; -1 for a graphic), Center_X and Center_Y, Center_Lon and Center_Lat, Area_Ha and Length_m (polygons) or Length_m (lines), all geodesic, and empty Treatment and Block fields ready for Add Random Numbers. Points, lines and polygons all work. With add the copies to the map as graphics checked the copies also become a graphics layer in the active map (in a script with no map this is skipped with a warning).
From the window. The Create Array along Axes window passes its selected graphic as Esri JSON in the source geometry parameter instead of input features, and draws the axes on the map; the geoprocessing tool it runs is this one, so the run is in History.

param.name: in_features
param.displayname: Input features (selection honored) or graphics layer

dialogReference.para: The features to copy, together as one group: a feature layer (its selection honored), a feature class, or a graphics layer (every graphic of one geometry type). Not needed when a source geometry is given.
Direction of the first axis. Copies forward go this way.
Space between neighboring copies along axis 1, on top of the source's extent; 0 = touching.
Meters, Feet, US survey feet, Yards, Kilometers or Miles, for both separations.

param.name: n_forward
param.displayname: Copies forward along axis 1 (not counting the original)

dialogReference.para: How many copies in the direction of the first bearing.
How many copies the opposite way.

param.name: out_fc
param.displayname: Output feature class (optional when adding graphics)

dialogReference.para: Where to write the copies (a geodatabase feature class or a shapefile). May be left empty when the copies are added as graphics.
Direction of the second axis; empty = perpendicular to the first.
Space between neighboring copies along the second axis.

param.name: n_right
param.displayname: Copies to the right along axis 2

dialogReference.para: How many copies in the direction of the second bearing (of the whole first-axis row).

param.name: n_left
param.displayname: Copies to the left along axis 2

dialogReference.para: How many copies the opposite way.

param.name: clip_features
param.displayname: Clip the copies to these polygons (selection honored)

dialogReference.para: Polygons to cut the copies to; copies entirely outside are dropped. A selection and a definition query are honored.

param.name: to_graphics
param.displayname: Also add the copies to the map as graphics

dialogReference.para: Checked: a graphics layer of the copies is added to the active map as well.

param.name: in_geometry
param.displayname: Source geometry as Esri JSON (used by the window instead of input features)

dialogReference.para: The Create Array along Axes window passes its selected graphic here. Scripts may pass any geometry's JSON (arcpy's Geometry.JSON) instead of input features.

scriptExample.title: Create Array along Axes example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: A 4 x 3 array of a selected plot polygon: three copies east of it with 5 m gaps, and the whole row copied twice to the south, clipped to the field.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path arcpy.management.MakeFeatureLayer(r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plots", "plot_lyr") arcpy.management.SelectLayerByAttribute("plot_lyr", "NEW_SELECTION", "Plot_ID = 'R1P1'") arcpy.jenness.CreateArrayAlongAxes( in_features="plot_lyr", bearing1=90, gap1=5, units1="Meters", n_forward=3, n_back=0, out_fc=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Plot_array", bearing2=180, gap2=5, n_right=2, n_left=0, clip_features=r"D:\data\trial.gdb\Fields", to_graphics=False)
